question: Wait — in northern summer, isn't Earth farther from the Sun? Why is it hotter then?

steps.title: Good question
steps.say: Distance isn't the cause: the orbit is almost a circle, and Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

ops.text:
Good question! The orbit is almost
a circle: the distance changes by
only about 3%. Earth is closest in
January, in northern winter.

steps.title: Perspective
steps.say: The picture is tilted to show the orbit, so distances in the drawing look different from real life.

ops.text:
Drawing is tilted for perspective —
the real orbit is almost circular.

steps.title: What really changes
steps.say: What changes is how directly sunlight hits the northern half: more direct when tilted toward the Sun, less direct when tilted away.

steps.title: Tilt, not distance
steps.say: So the tilt, not the distance, drives the seasons.

ops.text:
Tilt changes how directly
sunlight hits → seasons.
